screens.prompt: In B7, work out the North gross margin as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal, and wrap it in IFERROR so an empty region shows a blank.

require.message: The capstone has to survive a missing region: wrap the calculation in IFERROR.
The capstone totals by region: build the revenue with SUMIF.
The capstone reports margin to one decimal: use ROUND.

hints.func-iferror: IFERROR(value, "") goes on the outside, so a region with no revenue shows a blank instead of #DIV/0!.
hints.func-sumif: Total the North revenue and the North cost separately: SUM would mix in every region.
hints.func-round: The margin needs ROUND to one decimal; without it the cell shows a long string of digits.
hints.one-decimal: ROUND's second argument is the number of decimals, and this answer wants 1.
hints.require-ref: Match on the region column and add the revenue column, so the answer follows the table.
hints.value: Work in stages: North revenue, minus North cost, over North revenue, times 100. That is (2500 - 1380) / 2500 * 100 = 44.8.
hints.error: If the cell still shows an error, the division ran outside IFERROR, or IFERROR has no second argument to show when a region comes back empty.

screens.prompt: Open the workbook and read the gross margin in B7.

hints.value: B7 is the same IFERROR(ROUND(SUMIF...)) cell you wrote above, and the file recalculates it when it opens.

docs.explain:
SUMIF pulls the North rows out of each money column: revenue 1500 + 1000 comes to 2500 and cost 800 + 580 to 1380. Subtracting cost from revenue leaves 1120, and dividing that by revenue gives 0.448. Multiply by 100 and ROUND to one decimal for 44.8.

The reference answer nests three functions. SUMIF builds both totals, ROUND holds the margin at one decimal, and IFERROR wraps the result. A region with no revenue would divide by zero, and IFERROR(value,"") turns that error into a blank a chart can still plot.

Order inside the nest matters. ROUND sits inside IFERROR, so the guard wraps a finished number. Swapped, an empty region's division error reaches the cell before IFERROR can answer. Leave ROUND out and the margin arrives with a long tail of digits.

errors.text: A region with no revenue divides by zero, so the cell shows this until IFERROR catches it.
North is typed without quotes, so Excel reads it as a name and returns #NAME?.
Rounding the ratio to one decimal before multiplying by 100 gives 40 instead of 44.8.

docs.atWork: The region summary cell: two SUMIF totals, a ratio, a rounded figure and a blank where a region has no revenue.
docs.outcome: Total by region, divide to a margin percentage, and leave a blank where revenue is missing.
docs.teaches: SUMIF, ROUND and IFERROR nested in one formula

seo.title: Capstone in Excel: a gross margin cell
seo.description: SUMIF pulls the North rows, ROUND keeps one decimal and IFERROR turns a division error into a blank. The whole track in one formula, 44.8 percent.
